Geometric Distribution Object

Source: R/geometric_distrib.R
geometric_distrib.Rd

Creates a distribution object for the geometric distribution on \(\{0, 1, 2, \dots\}\), parametrized by its mean \(\mu\).

Usage

geometric_distrib(link_mu = log_link())

Arguments

link_mu

A link function object for \(\mu\). Defaults to log_link to ensure positivity.

Value

An S7 object of class GeometricDistrib.

Details

The distribution counts the failures before the first success, so the support includes zero and the success probability is \(p = 1/(1+\mu)\).

Probability mass function: $$P(Y = y; \mu) = \dfrac{1}{1+\mu}\left(\dfrac{\mu}{1+\mu}\right)^{y}$$

Score, observed and expected Hessian: $$\dfrac{\partial \ell}{\partial \mu} = \dfrac{y-\mu}{\mu(1+\mu)}, \qquad \dfrac{\partial^2 \ell}{\partial \mu^2} = -\dfrac{y}{\mu^2} + \dfrac{y+1}{(1+\mu)^2}, \qquad \mathbb{E}\left[\dfrac{\partial^2 \ell}{\partial \mu^2}\right] = -\dfrac{1}{\mu(1+\mu)}$$

Every order is the same expression evaluated at \(\mu\) and at \(1+\mu\), $$\ell^{(j)} = (-1)^{j-1}(j-1)!\left(\dfrac{y}{\mu^{j}} - \dfrac{y+1}{(1+\mu)^{j}}\right), \qquad \mathbb{E}[\ell^{(j)}] = (-1)^{j-1}(j-1)!\left(\mu^{1-j} - (1+\mu)^{1-j}\right)$$ so the expected orders are closed form and vanish at \(j = 1\).

Moments: mean \(\mu\), variance \(\mu(1+\mu)\), so the family is overdispersed relative to the Poisson at every mean.

Parameter domains:

  • \(\mu \in (0, +\infty)\)

The family is the negative binomial at \(\theta = 1\), so fixed(negbin2_distrib(), theta = 1) describes the same law and is used in the tests as an independent implementation.

See also

negbin2_distrib, poisson_distrib, exponential_distrib

Examples

d <- geometric_distrib()
d@params
#> [1] "mu"

theta <- list(mu = 2)
distrib_pdf(d, 0:4, theta)
#> [1] 0.33333333 0.22222222 0.14814815 0.09876543 0.06584362
distrib_gradient(d, 0:4, theta)
#> $mu
#> [1] -0.3333333 -0.1666667  0.0000000  0.1666667  0.3333333
#> 
c(mean = mean(d, theta), variance = variance(d, theta))
#>     mean variance 
#>        2        6
